Stranded Woman Turns the 2026 FAA Nationwide Ground Stop Into a 1,600-Mile Ford Bronco Road Trip
6 photos
Photo: @drtaraharding on Instagram
Tara Harding did not fly to Charlotte, North Carolina, with the intention of buying a Ford Bronco. She had a work trip to finish and a flight home to catch. As fate would have it, the FAA had other plans for her, grounding flights nationwide. Her airline repeatedly changed the departure arrangements, and alternatives began disappearing fast.
By the time Tara and two women from her team had exhausted their options, buying a body-on-frame SUV and driving 1,593 miles (2,564 kilometers) back to North Dakota sounded perfectly reasonable to her. This explains how a dealership visit turned into an unexpected nine-state road trip, followed by a surprising decision to keep the Sasquatch Package-equipped Outer Banks.
Harding explained the adventure on her Instagram, describing how the return flights had been rescheduled five times before the final cancellation. With the Federal Aviation Administration grounding flights due to a conflict between new telecom equipment and legacy air traffic control systems, getting out of North Carolina became way harder than simply finding another departure.
Tara and company spent plenty of time looking for alternatives, beginning with rental cars. The problem? None were available within a 4-hour radius. Trains and buses offered no workable solution either. The women also considered renting a U-Haul, but at that point, Harding's mother-in-law proposed buying a vehicle outright. Ka-ching! Surprisingly, Tara took the suggestion seriously.
She and her companions headed to Mark Ficken Ford (and Lincoln), a Charlotte dealer with a 4.6-star rating on Google Maps. Tara purchased the Bronco of her liking with help from salesman Jackson Weaver, whom she thanked publicly on Instagram.
A rather amusing sale, most definitely, especially when you remember that many Bronco customers spend a lot of time comparing trim levels, browsing accessories, and thinking whether a given option is worth the extra dollars.
Photo: @drtaraharding on Instagram The immediate priority was needing some wheels, and for some reason, I just remembered that scene from The Blues Brothers where Elwood says that it's 106 miles to Chicago, they got a full tank of gas, and half a pack of cigs in their 1974 Dodge Monaco. In my imagination, given the circumstances, Tara summoned her inner Jake when deciding to put money down on this nicely spec'd Bronco.
She had considered selling the off-road model after reaching North Dakota, with Tara even joking about putting the Bronco up for sale. She later admitted that a soft spot for it was developing, and who could blame her after so many miles of driving? After all, extraordinary circumstances brought them together.
Harding said the trip was filled with laughter and caffeine. The Ford Motor Company responded to one of Harding's posts, pointing out that such a trip is a great way to get to know her new ride. Speaking of which, the break-in period of a brand-new Bronco is 1,000 miles (a little over 1,600 kilometers).
Tara spent 12 hours in bed after the journey, and her husband also grew a soft spot for the Bronco. Before she even woke up, he had already taken the off-roader out for three drives. That changed the fate of the Bronco, with Tara confirming that her family will be keeping the Desert Sand-painted SUV .
